source.title: Disaggregation Reveals Hidden Training Dynamics: The Case of Agreement Attraction

record.tranche_reason: The study tracks grammatical benchmark performance across checkpoints of pretrained language models, extending training-dynamics analysis to text pretraining rather than small algorithmic datasets.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own accuracy trajectories on held-out agreement stimuli over training. It does not test small algorithmic datasets, training-set accuracy, or overfitting. Reported trends are qualitative; exact curve values are available only in plots.
record.test_reason: The study tracks subject-verb agreement accuracy across PolyPythia pretraining checkpoints (14M–410M) on held-out stimuli. It never measures training accuracy or memorization, so it cannot show generalization arriving long after the training set is fit. That is the defining feature of grokking in every version. Power et al. is cited only in a list of 'sudden learning' papers within a sudden-versus-gradual debate. The construct studied, condition-level 'hidden breakthroughs' and phase-like shifts from frequency to local-context heuristics, is related to grokking but different. It is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that grammatical learning is 'neither sudden nor gradual'. Instead it proceeds through a sequence of hidden breakthroughs that roughly track dependencies of increasing length: frequency, then the preceding word, possibly n-gram-like. Aggregate metrics hide these breakthroughs, which can lower as well as raise performance on some subsets. They describe the work as exploratory and warn against strong conclusions.
record.recipe_differences: This is an analysis of pretrained language-model checkpoints using subject-verb agreement accuracy on English stimuli, not training small networks on algorithmic datasets and tracking training-versus-test accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: Trajectories vary with model size, verb tokenization, and agreement condition; patterns are less stable in smaller models. Multi-token verb patterns generally occur later and have smaller performance decreases.

fits_no_version.finding: During Pythia pretraining, aggregate agreement accuracy looks gradual. Condition-level accuracy shows rapid, often non-monotonic shifts: a frequency preference first, then local-context (attraction) sensitivity, then broad improvement. Seed variation exists, and patterns are less stable in smaller models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In LM pretraining, gradual aggregate benchmark curves can hide sudden, non-monotonic condition-level 'hidden breakthroughs' driven by successive heuristics (unigram frequency, then local context).

record.peer_reviewed: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025)
record.problems: The authors characterize the analysis as exploratory and caution against strong conclusions without confirmatory analyses. Scope is limited to English subject-verb agreement with prepositional-phrase attractors and PolyPythia models. The text gives qualitative trajectory descriptions rather than exact values; plotted confidence intervals are shown.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result bearing on the tested versions was left out.

untested.parts: No algorithmic datasets, training accuracy or training-set-size manipulation.
No circuits, memorizing components or progress measures.
Text data is used, but there is no overfitting-then-generalization delay and no manipulation of initialization scale or weight norm.
Pretraining checkpoints are studied, but there is no training accuracy or memorization phase, so delayed generalization beyond overfitting is not assessed. No fine-tuning.
No weight decay, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
No algorithm identification across runs. Seed variation is reported only behaviourally.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T3 and its V3 supports and V4 limits_scope labels are removed. The rows measure held-out accuracy dynamics without any training-fit measure, so none bears on grokking as defined by the versions. Grokking is mentioned only by citation.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses language-model pretraining and grammatical stimuli, not small algorithmic datasets; it does not measure training accuracy, chance-level test accuracy after overfitting, or delay as training-set size changes.
No generalizing circuit or memorizing component is identified, measured, or removed, and no continuous mechanism-level progress measure is evaluated.
The study reports training trajectories on text but does not manipulate initialization scale or weight norm, or test a lazy-to-rich transition.

The study examines pretraining checkpoints and held-out grammatical stimuli, but does not measure training accuracy or establish overfitting before the test-accuracy changes. It does not study fine-tuning or report results from models larger than 410M parameters.
No low-norm bias, critical dataset size, or ungrokking is studied.
The study does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
The study does not test optimizer instability, floating-point limits, or controls for those proposed artifacts.

rows.subject: PolyPythia suite (Pythia 14M–410M)
rows.operation_detail: Measured agreement accuracy across checkpoints, averaged over all conditions.
rows.value: Little improvement, and in some cases a drop, until steps 256–512; performance then increases. The rise is smaller and more gradual for smaller models, begins later for Pythia 14M, and is faster and more complete for larger models.
rows.note: The text reports these trends qualitatively across model sizes; it does not give exact accuracy values or report training-set accuracy.
rows.check: Aggregate held-out accuracy rises from steps 256–512, but no training accuracy or overfitting phase is measured, so it cannot show delayed generalization beyond overfitting. The authors call the aggregate rise slow and gradual, not a jump. Not linked to V3 or V4.

rows.subject: PolyPythia suite (Pythia 14M–410M)
rows.operation_detail: Measured accuracy separately by agreement condition over training checkpoints.

conditions.value: plural target; plural target with plural attractor

rows.value: After an initial preference for the singular form, accuracy rises sharply for plural targets and plural targets with plural attractors around steps 128–512.
rows.note: The paper describes the trajectory but does not give exact accuracy values.
rows.check: A sharp rise in plural conditions around steps 128–512 reflects a shift from a frequency heuristic to local context. It is not delayed generalization after memorization. No training-set measure exists.

rows.subject: PolyPythia suite (Pythia 14M–410M)
rows.operation_detail: Measured accuracy separately by agreement condition over training checkpoints.
rows.value: The sharp rise seen for the other plural conditions is not seen in this condition.
rows.note: Exact values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: The absence of a rise in the plural-target/singular-attractor condition is an agreement-attraction pattern, not a grokking measure.

rows.subject: PolyPythia suite (Pythia 14M–410M)
rows.operation_detail: Measured accuracy separately by agreement condition over training checkpoints.
rows.value: Accuracy decreases sharply around the phase when plural-condition accuracy rises.
rows.note: The text identifies this as the agreement-attractor effect; exact values are not stated.
rows.check: An accuracy drop in the singular-target/plural-attractor condition is an attraction effect and is unrelated to delayed generalization.

rows.subject: PolyPythia suite (Pythia 14M–410M)
rows.operation_detail: Measured accuracy separately by agreement condition over training checkpoints.

conditions.value: singular target; singular target with singular attractor

rows.value: After an initial preference for plural verb forms, accuracy increases for singular targets and singular targets with singular attractors, followed by overall improvement.
rows.note: The report describes the pattern across models; exact values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: A condition-level heuristic shift for other single-token verbs. There is no overfitting baseline.

rows.subject: PolyPythia suite (Pythia 14M–410M)
rows.operation_detail: Measured accuracy separately by agreement condition over training checkpoints.
rows.value: Accuracy drops after the initial preference for plural forms, before overall performance improves.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative trajectory, not exact accuracy values.
rows.check: A condition-level drop due to attraction. It is not a grokking measure.

rows.subject: PolyPythia suite (Pythia 14M–410M)
rows.operation_detail: Measured accuracy separately by agreement condition over training checkpoints.

conditions.value: singular targets and singular targets with singular attractors; plural targets with singular attractors

rows.value: The general pattern is similar to that for other verbs: accuracy rises for singular and singular-with-singular-attractor conditions, with a corresponding decrease for plural targets with singular attractors. The changes generally occur later in training and the decrease is smaller.
rows.note: Several conditions are summarized together because the text reports the pattern jointly; exact values are not stated.
rows.check: The same multi-token verb pattern occurs later. It is a heuristic-phase trajectory, not delayed generalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: English agreement benchmark trajectories during PolyPythia text pretraining
reader_labels.reason: The reported held-out benchmark trajectories show condition-specific changes during pretraining; see R1–R7. The study does not test the proposed initialization-scale or weight-norm controls.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Pythia models from 14M to 410M parameters on English agreement stimuli
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy changes occur during pretraining, but the study does not show the overfitting-then-delayed-generalization pattern: it reports no training accuracy, and its results are on grammatical benchmark conditions rather than a grokking analysis; see R1–R7.
